nodes.label: Personal app store architecture
nodes.rationale: A calm shell hosting one mini-app per life area, added over time, rather than one monolithic life app - so each area can ship independently while the shell stays constant.

nodes.label: Principle: start small
nodes.rationale: Ship the smallest useful thing, then grow. Highest-priority guiding principle - it is what keeps the empty registry and the no-'coming soon'-tiles rule acceptable.

nodes.label: Principle: one design system
nodes.rationale: Every mini-app consumes the shared tokens and components so the whole hosted collection feels like one app rather than a launcher for strangers.

nodes.label: Principle: the contract is sacred
nodes.rationale: Adding a mini-app must never require editing shell internals - only registering a manifest. This is what makes the shell stable as apps accumulate, and it is why the shell renders tiles and routes from the registry and nothing else.

nodes.label: Principle: calm over clever
nodes.rationale: Soft, rounded, earthy, quiet - the app should feel like an exhale. Drives the no-sharp-corners rule, low warm shadows, 150-250ms motion, and reduced-motion support.

nodes.label: Tiswell tech stack
nodes.rationale: React 18 + TS on Vite, Tailwind v4 CSS-first tokens, vite-plugin-pwa, InstantDB, React Router with lazy per-mini-app routes, Cloudflare Pages, pnpm. Dexie/IndexedDB was the Phase 0-1 storage and survives only to migrate old devices.

nodes.label: Path aliases as platform boundaries
nodes.rationale: A single Vite app organized like a platform via @ui / @data / @miniapps / @shell aliases instead of a pnpm workspace monorepo, deliberately avoiding workspace overhead until it is actually needed. Manna aliases @ui and @data straight at these source folders, which is why src/data must never import from @shell.

nodes.label: MiniAppManifest
nodes.rationale: id, name, icon, accent, route, storageNamespace, component. Accent is a token name only, never a hex, so a mini-app cannot break the shared palette or the dark theme.

nodes.label: registry.ts (mini-app registry)
nodes.rationale: Home maps the registry to a Tile grid and App.tsx maps it to lazy Routes. Only live mini-apps appear - no 'coming soon' tiles, ever.

nodes.label: TiswellData interface
nodes.rationale: Every read and write in the app goes through list/get/put/remove/subscribe/snapshot/ready; no feature may import the backend directly. That single choke point is why swapping Dexie for InstantDB changed nothing above the data layer - the interface only grew subscribe/snapshot/ready, because a sync engine can say *when* data changed and a promise-only shape could not.

nodes.label: useRecords / useDataReady hooks
nodes.rationale: Callers subscribe through hooks instead of re-fetching after a write, because the sync engine already knows when data changed - including changes written by another origin or another device.

nodes.label: mirror.ts (in-memory read mirror)
nodes.rationale: Every read is served from an in-memory copy because db.queryOnce throws when offline. Being backend-free is also what makes it the part that can be unit tested.

nodes.label: instant.ts (Instant wiring + data singleton)
nodes.rationale: One auth subscription and one query subscription feeding the mirror, exporting the singleton `data: TiswellData`.

nodes.label: handshake.ts (postMessage session lending)
nodes.rationale: Tiswell holds the session and hands it to embedded apps over postMessage, origin-checked in both directions - one sign-in covers both origins.

nodes.label: migrate.ts (one-time Dexie drain)
nodes.rationale: Drains each origin's old Dexie database exactly once. local.ts and the dexie dependency exist only for this and should be deleted once every device has run it.

nodes.label: instant.schema.ts (records namespace)
nodes.rationale: One `records` namespace keyed "${ns}:${id}" because Instant keys entities by a single UUID and two namespaces may legitimately hold the same record id.

nodes.label: instant.perms.ts (owner-only rules)
nodes.rationale: Everything denied unless auth.id == data.owner. The app id ships in both client bundles by design, so these rules - not secrecy - are the guard.

nodes.label: Phase 2 shared database
nodes.rationale: Planned as Supabase plus a hand-rolled Dexie-Postgres mirror with updatedAt last-write-wins; shipped as InstantDB instead, so tombstones, LWW merge, pull cursors, and retry queues were never written at all. Tiswell and Manna sit on different origins where browser storage can never be shared, so a common backend was the only fix - and it bought one sign-in and cross-device sync on top of the original goal.

nodes.label: Manna as sibling app on its own origin
tokens.css design tokens
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth; components consume tokens only, never raw hex. Clay/umber/sage/sand neutrals, Quicksand display + Nunito Sans body, fully rounded controls. A literal hex, or a colour chosen only against light, is the way this system breaks.

nodes.label: Dark theme by token value swap
nodes.rationale: Token names are roles, not literal colours - clay-50 means app background, umber-900 means ink. One prefers-color-scheme block redeclares the custom properties and both apps flip with no `dark:` variant anywhere in the codebase. It follows the system, so nothing is stored and there is no flash of the wrong theme before React boots. Dark is warm brown-black, not neutral charcoal, so clay and umber still read as themselves.

nodes.label: raised / scrim / balance split tokens
nodes.rationale: Three tokens exist only because a role that is single-valued in light splits in two in dark. `raised` must go lighter while the background goes darkest, or the selected segment recedes. `scrim` is the one place ink is a surface; inverting it would flash the screen white at night. `balance` is Manna's balance card, which left to invert would become a glaring cream slab and instead becomes raised warm green. Do not collapse them back.

nodes.label: Quick-capture (the signature interaction)
nodes.rationale: A floating button visible in the shell and inside every mini-app opens a bottom sheet with one autofocused multiline input, saving straight to the `inbox` namespace. Capture must never require deciding where the thought belongs first.

nodes.label: Inbox
nodes.rationale: Reached from a header badge showing the unfiled count; newest-first with relative dates. 'File into app' stays disabled until mini-apps exist.

nodes.label: Home tile grid
nodes.rationale: With an empty registry it shows the Exhale mark, the words 'It is well.', and one line of copy - deliberately with no call to action.

nodes.label: Exhale mark
nodes.rationale: Clay-200 rounded square with three softening strokes in umber, umber-light, and sage at descending weight and opacity - the visual statement of 'calm over clever'. The SVG is the source all PNG icon sizes are regenerated from.
